newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt hands CVRD papers to court.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt hands CVRD papers to court.

text.p: Lawyers for the Brazilian government have handed in documentation requested by a judge considering a key appeal over the sale of miner Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a court spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman for the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) said Justice Democrito Reinaldo was expected to judge the case within 24 hours, possibly even on Monday.
"The Federal Advocacy has handed in the documents. The judge said he would judge in 24 hours. Over the weekend he told newspapers he might rule today," she said.
The government had been expected to hand in the documents Friday evening but lawyers arrived 20 minutes after the STJ closed and Justice Reinaldo refused to accept the papers.
A spokeswoman for the Federal Advocacy earlier said the delay may have benefited the government because its lawyers could continue working all weekend to prepare their case.
The auction of CVRD, originally scheduled for April 29, has been repeatedly put on hold because of court injunctions.
Justice Reinaldo was due to rule on a government petition that all the injunctions should be judged by a single tribunal due to a "conflict of interpretation" in lower courts.
The latest scheduled start for the auction was 1000 local/0900 EDT/1300 GMT Monday.
A spokeswoman for the National Development Bank (BNDES), which runs Brazil's privatization program, said the auction would take place as soon as Justice Reinaldo gave the green light.
